d85d9de9e65a: Niels Thomsen Silkjær had a large family of children, who grew up in and around Økjær. All of them carried Silkjær in their names, in varying forms: <t1>Nielsen Silkjær</t1>, <t2>Jensen Silkjær</t2>, or simply Silkjær. The first time anyone in the family is themselves recorded with the name in a census is in 1890, when the five eldest appear as Nielsen Silkjær, while the parents still appear as Niels Thomsen and Ane Jensen. That turns out to be decisive for everything that follows — for the name did not go only to the one who stayed. It went out into the world with every single child.

3f767d0fcad6: The eldest of the brothers and sisters has her own entry in Vort Sogns Historie — under her husband’s name. <t1>Ole Lauridsen</t1> was born in Husby on 29 May 1861 and died on 11 July 1916; so he was <t2>almost nineteen years older</t2> than his wife. They had <t3>eight children</t3>. The youngest, Ole, was born on 14 May 1916 and was barely two months old when his father died on 11 July. Ane Marie was then thirty-six and was left alone with the children — about the same age as her grandmother Anne Marie Jansdatter had been when death took her from her own children in 1863.

2349002f011d: Read that sentence together with chapter 2. The landscape that was not holiday country — poor soil, drifting sand, fishing from the open beach — was becoming it. And the first of the family to live off it was a widow who let out her fields, and her rooms to guests from the town. The land no longer gave enough. The view did.
